Rules / Cleanup

SK0260 The boolean expression says the same thing twice

A boolean expression that restates its own operand: a comparison against true or false, a double negation, a negated equality, a conditional returning the two boolean literals, or a &&/|| operand that cannot change the result.

CategoryCleanup
Default severitywarning
ScopeSemantic
Needs a compilationyes
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileyes
Fixyes, safe
Language version floor—
Since2.0
SupersedesDoubleNegationOperator, NegativeEqualityExpression, RedundantTernaryExpression, RedundantLogicalConditionalExpressionOperand

Why

Each shape asks the reader to evaluate a boolean twice. flag == true is flag with a comparison in front of it, and the comparison is the part a reader has to check is not =; !!ready reads as a typo until it is proved not to be; !(a == b) makes the reader invert an operator the language already has; found ? true : false is a conditional whose branches are the answer to the condition it was given; and enabled && true is an operand that was written to be true and stayed. ⚠ The shapes matter disproportionately for generated code: a model that assembles a condition from parts emits && true as the identity element of a fold, and emits ? true : false because most of its training data predates the habit of returning the condition.

⚠ Five ReSharper inspections, one concept: RedundantBoolCompare, DoubleNegationOperator, NegativeEqualityExpression, RedundantTernaryExpression and RedundantLogicalConditionalExpressionOperand. ReSharper rates the first four a warning and the last a suggestion; Skala reports the concept at warning.

⚠ Two of the five are hosted by Roslyn and three are not, and that was measured rather than assumed. Reflecting over Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CodeStyle in SDK 10.0.400 — 440 descriptors, read out of the assemblies because an error log cannot tell Hidden from absent — IDE0100 ("remove redundant equality") covers x == true and x != false, and IDE0075 ("simplify conditional expression") covers c ? true : false. Both are `IsEnabledByDefault: true` with `DefaultSeverity: Hidden`, so a plain dotnet build emits neither: the code-style analyzers are not loaded at all without EnforceCodeStyleInBuild, and even then a Hidden rule needs an explicit dotnet_diagnostic.IDExxxx.severity line before it says anything. Skala ships over them on the reasoning SK1005 already uses for IDE0161. ⚠ The other three are verified zeros, not unchecked ones: with all 120 IDE ids forced to warning and IDE0055, IDE0161, IDE0100, IDE0075 and IDE0380 all firing on the same compilation, nothing reported !!x, !(a == b) or x && true — and there was no AD0001, so no analyzer crashed silently past them.

Example

Instead of:

if (ready == true) { }
if (!!ready) { }
if (!(left == right)) { }

var found = index >= 0 ? true : false;
var ok = ready && true;

Write:

if (ready) { }
if (ready) { }
if (left != right) { }

var found = index >= 0;
var ok = ready;

When it does not fire

⚠ `bool?` is the false positive this rule is written around, and it defeats every shape at once. maybe == true is not maybe when maybe is bool?: the comparison is three-valued and yields false for null, so the rewrite turns a null into a compile error or, under an implicit conversion, into a different branch. Every shape therefore requires SpecialType.System_Boolean on the operand it reads — Nullable<bool> reports System_Nullable_T and is declined without a special case. ⚠ A user-defined `==` and a user-defined `!=` need not be each other's negation, so !(a == b) is reported only when the comparison binds to MethodKind.BuiltinOperator; a type that overloads equality is left alone even when the two operators do agree, because whether they agree is not a question the shape answers. ⚠ A `null` operand is declined and handed to `SK1010`: !(x == null) is that rule's is not null, and reporting both would put two ids on one span — the SK0244/SK6023 collision, avoided by reading the neighbour first rather than after. ⚠ `x && false` and `false && x` are deliberately not reported. The operand that cannot change the result is only && true and || false; deleting the other side drops an evaluation, which is a behaviour change and, where the dropped side has an effect, a defect worth its own finding rather than a cleanup. ⚠ A condition with a user-defined `operator true` is not a `bool`, so custom ? true : false keeps its conditional — removing it would change the expression's type from bool to the custom type. ⚠ The negated-equality fix is offered only where != can stand unparenthesised: under an operator that binds tighter than equality the finding is withdrawn rather than rewritten, because the alternative is emitting parentheses that SK0209 would then report as redundant, and two rules undoing each other is a skala fix that does not terminate. A comment or a directive inside the replaced span withdraws the finding, and the span is asked rather than the node — the defect #302 describes.
